The learned displays transfer without further optimization to the video encoder V-JEPA 2.1, which outperforms every EEG foundation model on both metrics on six of…

ov.problema: I modelli foundation per EEG (elettroencefalogramma) pre-addestrati su migliaia di ore di registrazioni trasferiscono male le loro feature congelate a compiti downstream, e questo trasferimento non migliora consistentemente con modelli più grandi o più dati. È importante trovare encoder migliori per segnali EEG.
ov.idea: Gli autori mostrano che un modello foundation per visione, che non ha mai visto EEG, è un encoder EEG congelato più forte di questi modelli specializzati, una volta che i segnali sono resi come immagini che un vision transformer può leggere. Il metodo, SeeEEG, mantiene il backbone di visione congelato e impara solo come visualizzare l'EEG: ogni canale occupa una riga dedicata di patch ed è disegnato come forma d'onda a guadagno fisso o come scalogramma la cui gamma di frequenze copre l'altezza della patch. I parametri di visualizzazione (montaggio, filtraggio, contrasto) sono inizializzati da…
ov.risultati: Confrontano SeeEEG con sette modelli foundation EEG su otto dataset clinici, del sonno, affettivi e di interfaccia cervello-computer, con ogni encoder congelato e testa di lettura identica. Con un DINOv3 ViT-B congelato, SeeEEG supera ogni modello foundation EEG in accuratezza bilanciata su tutti gli otto dataset e raggiunge un rango medio di 1.3 in Cohen kappa o AUROC, rispetto a 2.9 del miglior baseline, REVE. Le visualizzazioni apprese si trasferiscono senza ulteriore ottimizzazione ad altri dataset.
ov.limiti: Il testo non menziona limiti espliciti, ma il metodo richiede di convertire i segnali in immagini, il che potrebbe non essere ottimale per tutti i tipi di analisi EEG.

glossario.d: Elettroencefalogramma: registrazione dell'attività elettrica del cervello tramite elettrodi sul cuoio capelluto.
Modello di rete neurale per immagini che divide l'immagine in patch e le elabora come token.
Rappresentazione tempo-frequenza di un segnale, che mostra come le frequenze variano nel tempo.

2611.16968.abs: Purpose: Morphology is often regarded as relatively spared in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and is rarely modeled in connected speech. This study asked which morphological features distinguish speakers with AD from healthy controls, how well morphology classifies AD compared with other linguistic levels and BERT-based models, and whether the signal exceeds transcript length and vocabulary. Method: Fifty-five automatic measures in eight families, seven of them new and theory-motivated, were computed from participant speech in the ADReSS Cookie Theft descriptions (78 AD, 78 controls) and analyzed with group comparisons, equivalence tests, SHAP, family ablation, likelihood-ratio tests, feature-selection classifiers, and BERT-based models. The automatic measures were validated manually, and models were transferred to two other corpora. Results: Nineteen of 38 measures differed between groups: speakers with AD produced fewer suffixed and inflected words, shorter verbs and nouns, and fewer present-progressive but more past-tense forms (largest effect r = -0.42), whereas errors were rare and statistically equivalent between groups. Eight measures survived adjustment for length and lexical frequency. With test-set feature selection, morphology reached a macro-F1 of 0.85, on par with syntax and above fine-tuned BERT (0.80 over five seeds); fully cross-validated selection gave 0.62. Adding morphology to BERT improved AUC (0.91 vs. 0.89) but not macro-F1. Transfer was limited, although two thirds of the effects kept their direction in mild cognitive impairment. Conclusions: AD connected…

2611.16928.abs: Provably secure linguistic steganography hides a message inside text sampled from a language model, so that without the key, a stegotext is computationally indistinguishable from an honest model sample. Nearly every such scheme assumes the receiver can recompute the sender's token probabilities exactly bit for bit. We show this assumption is fragile: across three model families, bit-exact schemes decode almost none of our messages once the receiver's floating-point precision, quantization, or GPU architecture differs from the sender's, or even when the receiver merely scores a text in parallel versus one token at a time, with the same model, precision, and hardware held fixed. We present STEALTH, a scheme built for exactly this setting. The sender draws each token with an exponential race driven by keyed pseudorandom noise, so a receiver's probability mismatch flips a token only when the race is close; a rateless spinal code, decoded by beam search, absorbs the resulting flips without the sender and receiver ever agreeing on a single distribution. We prove stegotexts remain indistinguishable from honest samples under this construction. Empirically, STEALTH decodes every message we sent for every receiver in the sender's model family, at every precision and quantization level, on smaller models, and on a different GPU architecture. STEALTH is even robust across different model families with separate vocabularies and tokenizers, decoding every message we tested. Our approach carries far more payload per token than prior robust schemes, and trained steganalyzers and a…

2611.16925.abs: This report summarizes the Mobile Unified Multimodal Understanding (MUMU) track of the 8th Large-scale Video Object Segmentation (LSVOS) Challenge, held in conjunction with ECCV 2026. MUMU asks for a single unified model that jointly performs multi-concept image tagging over quality, scene, and event vocabularies, open-vocabulary object detection, and concise image captioning, within a budget of 0.5B parameters and 8 GB of peak inference memory. Submissions are ranked by a weighted task score scaled by an efficiency factor. We describe the tasks, rules, and evaluation protocol, report the final results, and review the methods of the top three teams. All three leading solutions build on the compact Florence-2-base model, but extend it in different ways: lightweight tagging heads with cross-task inference refinement, a shared low-rank adapter trained on coverage-aware multi-source data with task-dependent decoding, and a training-free pipeline that maps captions to tags and applies detection test-time augmentation. The results show that a compact prompt-based vision-language model can serve all three outputs when supervision, decoding, and cross-task cues are designed for each task, while open-vocabulary detection on novel categories remains the main bottleneck.

2611.17141.abs: A foundational principle of physics is that all coordinate systems are equally valid: the behavior of a PDE-governed system does not depend on the origin or orientation of the frame, nor on the units or mesh used to write it down, and neither should a surrogate model. Yet the neural surrogates with the lowest errors on today's aerodynamics benchmarks lack these invariances and fail under simple transformations of the same problem: for models trained on PDEs of cars in one pose (i.e., translation and rotation) and from one mesher, rotating the full PDE raises the surface-pressure error from 4% to more than 100%, and re-sampling its boundary raises it to about 30%. We introduce ISLA (Invariant Slice Attention), a slice-attention transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs in which no learned operation receives a coordinate and every sum over the boundary is a quadrature. Positions enter only as distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, lengths are measured in a unit computed from the boundary, and interior points query the boundary through a tree-accelerated learned kernel without influencing one another. With every boundary cell a token and an exact boundary read, ISLA is equivariant to rigid motions and reflections, invariant to the units of its declared data, and consistent under mesh refinement, while at every setting each query is independent of all other queries. On AeroZoo, 2,816 flows that vary in shape, size, speed, and boundary conditions, its mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1 and 3.3 times lower than any baseline's.…

2611.17114.abs: As autonomous AI agents increasingly interact in persistent populations, their collective capabilities and alignment depend not only on individual models, but also on the institutions governing their interactions. Yet AI research has largely focused on individual agents. In this Perspective, we argue that institutional design must become a distinct focus of AI research. Drawing on institutional political economy, social epistemology and organizational theory, we develop seven principles for designing AI institutions that sustain cooperation, enable reliable collective judgments and remain accountable to legitimate human purposes. These address reciprocal contributions, accountable authority, functional differentiation, epistemic pluralism, criticism and correction, human direction, and institutional adaptation. We illustrate their application through machine science, where autonomous research challenges institutions developed around human capabilities and constraints. We then propose an experimental research programme in which matched populations of AI agents operate under alternative institutional arrangements, and describe MoltJournal, an API-first journal for autonomous research agents, as an illustration of how such institutions can be made programmable and observable. Together, these contributions establish institutional design as a research agenda concerned not only with aligning autonomous agents, but with understanding how institutions can transform them into capable, reliable and accountable collectives.

2611.17108.abs: Memory decides which LLMs an edge device runs, and how fast: capacity on a $4$ GB Jetson Nano, bandwidth on an $8$ GB Jetson Orin Nano Super. Deployed formats (GPTQ, AWQ, $\texttt{llama.cpp}$'s K- and I-quants) spend equal bits on every integer code of a matrix, although the codes are far from uniform. $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ keeps these formats but tunes GPTQ so the codes compress, Huffman-codes them losslessly in interleaved lanes, and decodes them on demand in a small unit between DRAM and L2, so GPU kernels run unchanged and DRAM moves only coded bytes. At $1\%$ and $3.5\%$ perplexity budgets, coded Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B and SmolLM-1.7B are $5.7-31.4\%$ smaller than the best $\texttt{llama.cpp}$ format. A bit-exact $0.21$ mm$^2$ ASIC decoder unit ($1$ GHz, $7$ nm) cuts Orin latency and energy per token by up to $36\%$ and $38\%$ ($54\%$ and $44\%$ with prompt-lookup speculation). On the Nano, $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ needs $58-64\%$ less time and $53-57\%$ less energy per token than CPU $\texttt{llama.cpp}$, and runs a streamed Mistral-7B 6.6$\times$ faster at $3.89$ bits per weight. A Huffman decoder beats an rANS decoder in rate and area at equal throughput; the ASIC decoder unit runs bit-exact on a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA (AMD ZCU102).

ov.problema: Sui dispositivi edge (come Jetson Nano) la memoria limita quali LLM possono girare e quanto velocemente. I formati di quantizzazione esistenti usano bit uguali per ogni codice, anche se i codici non sono uniformi.
ov.idea: LazyWeights mantiene i formati esistenti ma regola GPTQ per comprimere i codici, li codifica con Huffman senza perdita in corsie interlacciate e li decodifica su richiesta in una piccola unità tra DRAM e L2. I kernel GPU restano invariati e la DRAM muove solo byte codificati.
ov.risultati: A budget di perplessità dell'1% e 3,5%, i modelli Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B e SmolLM-1.7B sono dal 5,7% al 31,4% più piccoli del miglior formato llama.cpp. Un decoder ASIC bit-exact da 0,21 mm² (1 GHz, 7 nm) riduce latenza ed energia per token fino al 36% e 38% su Orin (54% e 44% con speculazione prompt-lookup). Su Nano serve il 58-64% in meno di tempo e il 53-57% in meno di energia per token rispetto a llama.cpp su CPU, e Mistral-7B in streaming gira 6,6 volte più veloce a 3,89 bit per peso.
ov.limiti: Richiede un'unità di decodifica hardware dedicata per i guadagni massimi; i risultati su GPU senza ASIC non sono riportati.

glossario.d: Riduzione della precisione dei pesi per comprimere il modello.
Metodo di compressione senza perdita che assegna codici più corti ai simboli più frequenti.
Circuito integrato progettato per uno scopo specifico.

2611.16856.abs: Federated Learning (FL) with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) enables efficient adaptation of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet its energy and carbon costs across hardware remain poorly understood. We evaluated federated Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) fine-tuning on NVIDIA A40, RTX 6000 Ada, and A100 GPUs using a $2^2$ full factorial design with 135M/360M models and 10/100 local steps. CodeCarbon tracked energy and estimated CO$_2$-equivalent emissions. Descriptive allocation of variation assigned 84.8-91.2% of energy and emissions variation to local steps within these ranges. On A40 and RTX 6000 Ada, configurations with fewer steps achieved comparable accuracy with roughly 6-8-fold lower energy consumption and higher accuracy per kWh. These findings support smaller local budgets for energy-efficient federated fine-tuning within the evaluated setting.

2611.17128.abs: Smaller language models (SLMs) make it feasible to deploy clinical natural language processing where large proprietary models are too costly, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning allows them to be specialised on commodity hardware. One obstacle persists after training: on medical tasks these models answer at far greater length than the clinical question requires. In clinical decision support and point-of-care use, where time is short, such verbosity is hard to act on even when the underlying reasoning is sound. Existing length-control methods depend on preference optimisation, reward models, or proprietary teachers that undercut the accessibility making SLMs attractive. We introduce Parameter-Efficient Conciseness Adaptation (PECA), which adds a single differentiable conciseness term to the QLoRA supervised fine-tuning objective. Because the token count is discrete and non-differentiable, PECA instead raises the end-of-sequence probability once generation exceeds a token budget, a smooth signal optimised during ordinary training, with no preference data, no auxiliary model, and a single commodity GPU. On a 1.7-billion-parameter model fine-tuned on the medical-o1-reasoning-SFT corpus, PECA reduces mean response length by 72.8% while improving multiple-choice diagnostic accuracy from 40.8% to 44.0%. A sweep over the conciseness strength traces an interpretable accuracy-to-length frontier for balancing brevity and diagnostic completeness.

2611.17052.abs: LLM-based peer review is now used at production scale, but its evaluation remains limited. We introduce a benchmark that injects objective, localisable errors of four types (general issues, mathematics, numerics, citations) at three severity levels into real papers and measures each reviewer's detection rate by error type and severity, together with its false-positive rate on clean copies. We also present Skepthical, a multi-agent reviewer that verifies citation-backed claims by retrieving the cited papers, mathematics with computer algebra, and numerical claims with executed code. We apply the benchmark to two corpora of 15 recent arXiv preprints each, one in astrophysics and one in machine learning (ML), injecting a total of 357 errors, and evaluate twelve reviewer systems: six single-LLM reviewers, two Claude Code configurations, three publicly available reviewers, and Skepthical. The choice of model has the largest impact on detection rate: given the same prompt, three frontier LLMs differ by about 50 percentage points in total detection on both corpora. Tools and scaffolding help when they contribute what the model cannot supply on its own. In particular, on astrophysics, Claude Code improves on a single Claude call in mathematics and numerics detection, and enforced citation retrieval gives Skepthical the highest citation error detection rate of all systems by a large margin. This citation lead, however, is not observed on ML, where the models appear to know the literature better and Skepthical's citation detection rate is statistically indistinguishable from that of…

ov.problema: L'uso di LLM per la revisione tra pari è ormai su larga scala, ma la loro valutazione è limitata. È importante misurare quanto siano bravi a individuare errori oggettivi e localizzabili in articoli scientifici reali.
ov.idea: Gli autori introducono un benchmark che inietta errori di quattro tipi (generali, matematici, numerici, citazioni) a tre livelli di gravità in articoli reali e misura il tasso di rilevamento per tipo e gravità, insieme al tasso di falsi positivi su copie pulite. Presentano anche Skepthical, un revisore multi-agente che verifica affermazioni supportate da citazioni recuperando gli articoli citati, controlla la matematica con algebra computazionale e le affermazioni numeriche eseguendo codice.
ov.risultati: Applicano il benchmark a due corpora di 15 preprint arXiv ciascuno (astrofisica e ML), iniettando 357 errori, e valutano dodici sistemi di revisione. La scelta del modello ha l'impatto maggiore: tre LLM frontier differiscono di circa 50 punti percentuali nel rilevamento totale. Strumenti e scaffolding aiutano quando forniscono ciò che il modello non può fare da solo. In astrofisica, Claude Code migliora il rilevamento di matematica e numerica rispetto a una singola chiamata, e il recupero forzato delle citazioni dà a Skepthical il più alto tasso di rilevamento di errori di citazione, con un…
ov.limiti: Il vantaggio di Skepthical nel rilevamento di errori di citazione non si generalizza al dominio ML, suggerendo una dipendenza dal dominio.

glossario.d: Processo di valutazione di un articolo scientifico da parte di esperti del settore prima della pubblicazione.
Struttura di supporto che guida un modello LLM attraverso passaggi intermedi per migliorare le prestazioni.

2611.17048.abs: Most AI assistants respond only when prompted, remaining silent even when events in the video stream offer meaningful opportunities for conversation. To move beyond purely user-driven interaction, we present AURA 2.0, a streaming video large language model that introduces three core upgrades to AURA. The key advance is Model-Initiated Conversation (MIC), which enables the model to identify topics worth discussing in the evolving visual stream and initiate conversations at appropriate moments without a user query. Stream-Aware Tool Calling (SATC) enables the model to invoke external tools using the current visual and conversational context and incorporate returned information into the ongoing interaction. Interactive Visual Grounding (IVG) supports visual grounding in both user inputs and model outputs. The model can identify objects marked by users on video frames and produce frame-aligned bounding boxes to link its responses to specific objects and regions. To develop these capabilities, we construct a dedicated streaming interaction dataset and adopt a three-stage training scheme to integrate the new behaviors with AURA's existing streaming interaction abilities. We further incorporate Long-Horizon Interaction Memory (LHIM) to maintain contextual continuity over extended video streams. Evaluations on public streaming benchmarks show that AURA 2.0 achieves leading performance among open-source streaming models, while targeted evaluations further validate its new interaction capabilities. We open-source the model weights and inference code.

2611.17041.abs: Multi-agent deep-research systems use delegation to parallelize search and keep long tool traces out of the main agent's context. Yet delegation helps only when task allocation and subtask execution are coordinated: the main agent must issue useful subtasks, while subagents must return reliable evidence. Existing training either optimizes only the main agent or broadcasts the same team advantage to all agents, which can reward misleading subagent reports and penalize useful ones. We introduce LEAD-RL (Learning Effective Agent Delegation with Reinforcement Learning), a joint main-agent-subagent training framework with contribution-aware credit assignment. A training-time rubric evaluates the research utility of each subagent report and gates its inherited team advantage, while final-answer correctness remains the only team reward; no token, step, or speedup reward is used. Across five benchmarks and two model families, LEAD-RL improves answer quality. On BrowseComp, it improves accuracy by 2.49 percentage points and reduces critical-path cost by 24.5% over joint training with shared team credit. During validation, accuracy increases by 6.78 points at approximately constant critical-path cost. These results show that contribution-aware credit assignment improves the quality-efficiency trade-off of multi-agent deep research.

ov.problema: I sistemi multi-agente di deep research usano la delega per parallelizzare la ricerca e tenere le lunghe tracce di tool fuori dal contesto dell'agente principale. Ma la delega aiuta solo se allocazione dei task ed esecuzione dei subtask sono coordinate: l'agente principale deve emettere subtask utili e i subagenti devono restituire evidenze affidabili. L'addestramento esistente o ottimizza solo l'agente principale o assegna lo stesso vantaggio di squadra a tutti, premiando report fuorvianti e penalizzando quelli utili.
ov.idea: LEAD-RL (Learning Effective Agent Delegation with Reinforcement Learning) è un framework di addestramento congiunto agente principale-subagenti con credit assignment (assegnazione del merito) basato sul contributo. Una rubrica a tempo di training valuta l'utilità di ricerca di ogni report dei subagenti e controlla il vantaggio di squadra ereditato, mentre la correttezza della risposta finale resta l'unico reward di squadra; non si usano reward per token, passi o velocità.
ov.risultati: Su cinque benchmark e due famiglie di modelli, LEAD-RL migliora la qualità delle risposte. Su BrowseComp, aumenta l'accuratezza di 2.49 punti percentuali e riduce il costo del percorso critico del 24.5% rispetto all'addestramento congiunto con credito di squadra condiviso. In validazione, l'accuratezza aumenta di 6.78 punti a costo del percorso critico approssimativamente costante.
ov.limiti: La rubrica di valutazione dei report è usata solo in training e potrebbe non catturare tutte le sfumature di utilità; i risultati sono su benchmark specifici.

glossario.d: Attribuzione del merito o colpa alle azioni che hanno contribuito al risultato.
Costo lungo il percorso critico, cioè la sequenza più lunga di dipendenze.
Criterio di valutazione strutturato usato per assegnare punteggi.

2611.16895.abs: Post-training of large language models typically combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with preference-based fine-tuning such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Human-annotated and synthetically generated preference data differ substantially in per-sample cost, but prior work typically holds sample count fixed when comparing the two. In this work, we explicitly study the interplay between cost and performance by comparing the effect of post-training with human and synthetic preference data under a fixed, dollar-matched annotation budget. We train and evaluate multiple base model families across helpfulness and summarization tasks. We find that synthetic data is far more cost-efficient at low-to-moderate budgets, achieving high win rates with as little as \$200--\$400. On helpfulness, human data closes the gap only at budgets roughly two orders of magnitude larger; on summarization, it does not close the gap at any tested budget. We also find that human-annotated data varies in reliability: one widely used human preference source substantially underperforms another, and the gap persists even after standard remedies such as domain restriction and deduplication.

2611.16662.abs: Theory of Mind (ToM), the ability to infer mental states in others, is pivotal for human social cognition. Existing evaluations of ToM in large language models (LLMs) mainly focus on static belief attribution and false-belief reasoning, leaving a critical aspect of social reasoning underexplored: can LLMs decide whether perceptual evidence is sufficient to justify another person's belief revision? To address this gap, we present MuSeToM, a human-validated, text-based benchmark for evaluating epistemic belief revision in ToM reasoning. MuSeToM contains 2,415 instances adapted from BigToM and OpenToM, with textual cues spanning six sensory categories, and tests whether models can determine when a protagonist should revise a belief and infer the resulting updated belief state. Using MuSeToM, we systematically evaluate state-of-the-art LLMs under direct and chain-of-thought prompting, revealing a pronounced dissonance: while models often detect that a belief may change, they struggle to identify the updated belief and frequently over-update on perceptually salient but epistemically insufficient cues.

2611.16647.abs: Multimodal depression screening estimates risk from speech, visual behavior and language. Current methods mainly predict labels, with limited evidence of departures from a non-depressed reference. Recording-level supervision also leaves fine-grained emotional dynamics unannotated. Motivated by emotional inertia, the persistence of affect, InertiaMPDD learns healthy next-state patterns using a world-model-inspired latent predictor. Using pretrained multimodal representations, it predicts from observed history and context. Reference deviation, residual decay rate and a Jacobian spectral descriptor form reference-derived emotional dynamics descriptors, evaluated as candidate proxy biomarkers for standalone screening and personalized decision correction. Across five cohorts from four datasets, fusion reaches 98.41% F1 on D-Vlog and 84.98% on LMVD. Standalone descriptors outperform fixed additive fusion on MPDD but discriminate weakly on AVEC2014. These findings distinguish reference informativeness from fusion benefit and reveal context-dependent utility.

2611.16621.abs: Most sign languages have no annotated corpus, only small dictionaries with one or a few example videos per sign. This study examines how well a pose encoder trained on a single sign language serves such languages without any target-language training. An encoder trained with metric learning on American Sign Language (ASL-Citizen) is evaluated frozen on six datasets of Turkish, Russian, Indian, Argentinian, Pakistani and Sri Lankan sign languages, with one or four clips per sign enrolled and, where signer identities are available, the query's signer excluded from the gallery. With one enrolled clip, the encoder retrieves the correct sign first in 36.4-80.7 % of queries, against 16.0-69.6 % for the best learning-free method (angle-based dynamic time warping) and a six-target mean of 39.3 % for an ASL-trained OpenHands graph network. In a crossed ablation of the encoder (embedding geometry, aggregation of body and hand embeddings, training objective, and attention between articulators), two choices matter: a per-pair InfoNCE objective outperforms supervised contrastive and cross-entropy training, and blocking attention between body, left hand and right hand inside the encoder raises accuracy by up to 5.1 points. The best configuration reaches 68.0 % one-shot accuracy (59.0 % for the reference encoder). On CISLR, an Indian Sign Language dictionary of 4,765 words with one video per word, the encoders find the correct word first for 17.3-19.0 % of queries, above the 16.8 % of the original RGB baseline. Over eight seeds with the joint encoder, spherical, Euclidean and hyperbolic…

2611.16897.abs: We introduce TokenStream, an optimization-based framework that composes independently learned subject identities in text-to-video generation without a reference-video training dataset or joint optimization of each new subject combination. Learning from a single reference image makes subject appearance difficult to separate from static-image bias, while merging independently trained adapters can mix identities. Token-wise LoRA (ToRA) restricts low-rank updates to the cross-attention value projections of subject-associated text tokens, providing a separate adaptation path for each subject. A T2V-guided stream copies queries and keys from the frozen base model during early denoising to reuse its layout and motion priors while retaining personalized values. We also introduce Multi-DB, a 30-subject, 122-prompt benchmark with appearance-free prompts and varied interactions. On Multi-DB at 1.3B, TokenStream improves identity preservation from 0.422 for DreamBooth to 0.467 and textual alignment from 0.652 to 0.688.

2611.16956.abs: General-purpose language models are trained mostly on English: over open models we review, at most, non-English pretraining data makes up only a 12% share. Models built for European languages give them far more, but score well below general-purpose models of the same size. A common concern is that, in small models, languages compete for capacity. We present Lara Mini base, a model trained from scratch on 6T tokens in English and 44 other languages, which together cover all 24 official languages of the European Union. As training progresses, the 44 other languages together come to outweigh English. To give these languages enough capacity at low cost, Lara Mini base uses a mixture of experts architecture with 7.2B total and 0.6B active parameters. Among open base models with up to 2B active parameters, it achieves the highest average score across standard English, multilingual, math, and code benchmarks, ahead of models trained on 4 to 6 times as many tokens. Its margin is largest on multilingual benchmarks in the languages it supports and on math benchmarks. It supports contexts of up to 128k tokens. We find that our MoE architecture reduces capacity competition between languages. For a single user on one GPU, without quantization, it generates text at least 1.8 times faster than any model with a higher average score. We release the weights of Lara Mini base under the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 license. In addition, we will release T-HellaSwag, a higher-quality machine translation of the commonsense reasoning benchmark HellaSwag into 110 language variants.

2611.17072.abs: Fine-tuning foundation models on financial data has a wide range of applications, including identifying event types from news, monitoring risk and compliance language, and answering questions over filings and earnings calls. In this setting, the main challenge is to improve task performance without degrading the generalization capabilities of the model. In this paper, we present an extensive set of ablations for fine-tuning Qwen3-8B with low-rank adaptation (LoRA). We compare three training regimes: (1) response-only LoRA, where the supervised response is the label alone; (2) single-adapter reasoning, where reasoning traces from a teacher model are included alongside the labels in the training loss; and (3) dual-adapter composite training, where separate LoRA adapters are trained on traces and labels. Response-only LoRA improves in-domain performance and leaves general capabilities near those of the frozen model. The in-domain change is largest for calibration and argmax accuracy. Under single-adapter reasoning, the in-domain metrics remain behind those of the response-only regime, while MMLU-Pro can rise slightly and the other retention benchmarks stay within ordinary variation. Dual-adapter composite training remains on the same side of this comparison and yields no further gain. Finally, we compress the teacher traces by summarizing them before training, and show that shorter summaries move calibration toward the response-only regime without reaching it.

ov.problema: Adattare modelli foundation su dati finanziari è utile per classificare eventi, monitorare rischi e rispondere a domande, ma la sfida è migliorare le prestazioni specifiche senza degradare le capacità generali del modello.
ov.idea: Gli autori conducono un ampio studio di ablazione su Qwen3-8B con LoRA, confrontando tre regimi: (1) LoRA solo risposta (il target è solo l'etichetta), (2) LoRA con ragionamento a singolo adattatore (tracce di ragionamento di un insegnante incluse nella loss), (3) training composito a doppio adattatore (adattatori separati per tracce ed etichette). Inoltre comprimono le tracce dell'insegnante riassumendole prima dell'addestramento.
ov.risultati: LoRA solo risposta migliora le prestazioni in-domain e lascia le capacità generali vicine a quelle del modello congelato; il cambiamento in-domain è massimo per calibrazione e accuratezza argmax. Con ragionamento a singolo adattatore, le metriche in-domain restano dietro al regime solo risposta, mentre MMLU-Pro può salire leggermente e gli altri benchmark di ritenzione restano nella variazione ordinaria. Il training composito a doppio adattatore non porta ulteriori guadagni. Le tracce compresse spostano la calibrazione verso il regime solo risposta senza raggiungerlo.

glossario.d: Tecnica di fine-tuning efficiente che aggiunge piccoli adattatori ai pesi.
Esperimento che rimuove o varia componenti per studiarne l'effetto.
Quanto le probabilità predette riflettono l'accuratezza reale.

2611.16693.abs: Mobile GUI agents read the screen of a phone and operate apps on a user's behalf to complete multi-step tasks such as online shopping or messaging. Because the agent acts on whatever the screen shows, an attacker can embed malicious instructions into ordinary UI content and redirect its actions. We refer to this threat as environmental injection attack (EIA). Existing benchmarks measure this risk by pinning hand-crafted payloads to a fixed step of a fixed task. This approach faces two limitations. First, each payload is bound to one task in one app and does not transfer without manual redesign. Second, agents given the same task may follow different routes, so an agent that never reaches the injected page is recorded as safe without being tested. This insufficient test coverage can cause fixed-point benchmarks to underestimate the security risk of deployed mobile agents. In this work, we propose MobileProbe, a trajectory-aware red-teaming framework that evaluates mobile agents adaptively. MobileProbe discovers attacker-controllable content surfaces through automated pentesting, localizes vulnerable decision points along the agent's trajectory, and iteratively refines context-aware payloads through a surrogate-filtered evolutionary loop. We construct a benchmark of 83 long-horizon attack instances spanning 12 mobile applications. Each is annotated with a Confidentiality, Integrity, or Availability (CIA) attack goal to cover the principal categories of security threats facing mobile agents. On three representative agent architectures, MobileProbe attains higher attack…

2611.17129.abs: Federated learning experiments can produce reasonable-looking results even when the experiment implementation differs from the intended experimental protocol. Small errors in configuration, data partitioning, aggregation, randomness, evaluation, or checkpoint recovery may therefore affect a comparison without causing the program to fail. We present FedBrew, a research codebase for controlled and reproducible federated learning experiments. Its focus is controlled simulation with checks of specified conditions of the intended experimental protocol. FedBrew uses configuration checks, identifiable client data partitions, checkpoint recovery checks, self-describing run records, and development-time checks of scientific conditions. These checks assess, for example, whether client partitions are disjoint and exhaustive and aggregation weights match the prescribed rule; numerical and recovery checks examine non-finite client model states and interrupted runs. The same structure also provides clear extension points and automated checks for new algorithms, datasets, models, and tasks, whether they are added by researchers or AI coding agents. FedBrew therefore supports reproducible and inspectable FL experiments through checks of specified software and scientific conditions and the run records associated with reported results.

2611.17115.abs: Enforcement defenses against prompt injection, such as CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard and DRIFT, ask the agent's own model to write a security artifact (a program, a privilege policy, a dependency graph or a constraint list) that code then enforces. We ask whether small language model (SLM) agents can be trusted to write these artifacts. Across 15 open-weight models, 13 of them between 1.7B and 12B parameters, they cannot: the policies, graphs and constraints that the agent's model writes admit attacks on 14 (Progent), 13 (IPIGuard) and 11 (DRIFT) of the models, and CaMeL's programs fail to run in up to 68% of episodes. We present CapLite, which derives its policy from the tool schemas, commits the write calls before any tool result is read, and admits a write only if every argument that decides whom or what it affects is stated in the user's request. This guarantees write integrity: injected text cannot add a write, and no write reaches a recipient, amount, object or destination that the user did not state. No attack succeeds in 13,935 attacked AgentDojo episodes. CapLite reaches utility under attack comparable to CaMeL's (29.0% vs. 27.2%) with fewer tokens than every other enforcement defense and than the undefended agent: 17.1k per episode, 18% of CaMeL's, and the highest utility per token of all enforcement defenses.

ov.problema: Le difese contro prompt injection come CaMeL, Progent, IPIGuard e DRIFT chiedono al modello dell'agente di scrivere un artefatto di sicurezza (programma, policy, grafo o lista di vincoli) che poi viene applicato dal codice. Ci si chiede se gli agenti basati su small language model (SLM) possano essere affidabili in questo.
ov.idea: CapLite deriva la policy dagli schemi degli strumenti, impegna le chiamate di scrittura prima di leggere qualsiasi risultato e ammette una scrittura solo se ogni argomento che decide chi o cosa influenza è dichiarato nella richiesta dell'utente. Questo garantisce l'integrità delle scritture: testo iniettato non può aggiungere scritture e nessuna scrittura raggiunge destinatari, importi, oggetti o destinazioni non dichiarati dall'utente.
ov.risultati: Su 15 modelli open-weight (13 tra 1.7B e 12B parametri), le policy, grafi e vincoli scritti dal modello dell'agente subiscono attacchi su 14 (Progent), 13 (IPIGuard) e 11 (DRIFT) modelli, e i programmi di CaMeL falliscono l'esecuzione fino al 68% degli episodi. CapLite non subisce attacchi riusciti in 13.935 episodi attaccati di AgentDojo. Raggiunge utilità sotto attacco comparabile a CaMeL (29.0% vs 27.2%) con meno token di ogni altra difesa enforcement e dell'agente non difeso: 17.1k per episodio, 18% di CaMeL, e la più alta utilità per token.
ov.limiti: La garanzia di integrità vale solo per le scritture; altre forme di attacco o utilità in scenari non testati non sono coperte.

glossario.d: Attacco che inserisce istruzioni malevole nel testo per manipolare l'agente.
Small Language Model: modello linguistico di piccole dimensioni.
Benchmark per valutare sicurezza e utilità di agenti linguistici.

2611.17101.abs: P300-based brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) enable communication by decoding stimulus-evoked EEG responses into character selections without requiring voluntary motor output. Reliable P300 detection remains difficult because of low response amplitude and signal-to-noise ratio, while practical spellers require accurate character selection with few stimulus repetitions and low computational cost. We propose a compact deep learning architecture that combines xDAWN spatial filtering for event-related potential enhancement and dimensionality reduction, a fixed frequency-selective filter bank, and convolutional feature learning for spatio-temporal EEG decoding. Depthwise-separable convolutions and progressive average pooling reduce computational complexity while retaining discriminative temporal information. The resulting target/non-target classifier contains only 5,100 trainable parameters. We evaluated the model on two public benchmarks, BCI Competition II Dataset IIb and BCI Competition III Dataset II, and compared it with established P300 decoding methods across different numbers of stimulus repetitions. The model achieved an information transfer rate of 17.8 bits/min with two repetitions on BCI Competition III and 40.5 bits/min on BCI Competition II, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-speed trade-off. These results suggest that combining domain-informed spatial and spectral priors with compact neural networks can support efficient P300 decoding for EEG-based BCI communication.

2611.17068.abs: Program evolution provides a promising approach to discover agent memory designs and study the choices underlying their effectiveness. We introduce MAPE, a framework that evolves whole memory programs from minimal seeds through a standardized lifecycle interface and an iterative diagnosis-proposal loop. Experiments on LoCoMo and LongMemEval yield an absolute accuracy gain of up to 12% over manually designed baselines at 35% of the serving cost, with further evaluations supporting transfer across serving backbones and benchmarks. Empirical analyses and ablations identify and validate two recurring design patterns: retaining raw conversations as retrievable evidence preserves details omitted from extracted memories, while composing retrieved evidence according to query intent helps the answering model use it effectively. Transplanting the composition module into five existing memory systems improves accuracy across all five. Beyond these patterns, the search objective shapes where computation goes: optimizing serving cost alongside accuracy shifts computation from LLM-based memory construction to selective processing at query time while retaining competitive accuracy. Together, these findings offer empirical lessons for agent memory design. Code is available at https://github.com/ash-ding/MAPE.

ov.problema: Progettare la memoria degli agenti è difficile: servono scelte efficaci su cosa memorizzare e come recuperarlo. I progetti manuali sono costosi e non sempre ottimali.
ov.idea: MAPE evolve interi programmi di memoria da semi minimali attraverso un'interfaccia standardizzata e un ciclo iterativo di diagnosi e proposta. L'evoluzione scopre automaticamente design efficaci.
ov.risultati: Su LoCoMo e LongMemEval si ottiene un guadagno assoluto di accuratezza fino al 12% rispetto a baseline progettate a mano, con il 35% del costo di servizio. Due pattern ricorrenti emergono: conservare le conversazioni grezze come evidenza recuperabile e comporre l'evidenza in base all'intento della query. Il modulo di composizione migliora l'accuratezza in cinque sistemi di memoria esistenti.
ov.limiti: Il testo non specifica la generalità oltre i benchmark testati né i costi di evoluzione.

glossario.d: Evoluzione automatica di programmi tramite mutazioni e selezione.
Benchmark per la memoria a lungo termine negli agenti conversazionali.

2611.17059.abs: Online conformal risk control (OCRC) enables reliable uncertainty quantification in machine learning by converting model outputs into prediction sets with long-term risk guarantees. These guarantees, however, hinge on the assumption that the loss of each round is revealed immediately and losslessly. In practice, feedback may be delayed, and limited resources may prevent tracking all pending predictions, causing some feedback to be lost. To address this challenge, we develop capacity-aware OCRC (CA-OCRC), a framework that jointly determines how to allocate limited tracking feedback capacity and how to construct prediction sets. CA-OCRC is based on a randomized tracking policy that samples a proxy delay to decide whether, and for how long, feedback for the current round is tracked. CA-OCRC updates the prediction sets via inverse probability weighting, compensating for the possibility of feedback lost due to delays and limited tracking capacity. We analyze risk bounds for both arbitrary and stochastic delays, revealing a trade-off between receiving more feedback and avoiding capacity saturation. Building on these bounds, we optimize the proxy delay distribution, showing scaling laws for the tracking capacity that ensure the same long-term risk as OCRC with unlimited feedback. Experiments on medical imaging, natural language processing, computer vision, and wireless communications show the effectiveness of CA-OCRC as compared to existing OCRC mechanisms.

2611.17019.abs: Layer-local self-supervised objectives remove the backward pass between layers, but almost all still compute their loss over a batch of samples and are therefore local in space but not in time. We introduce Temporal Regularized Learning (TeReL), a spatially and temporally local learning rule for self-supervised representation learning from sequential input streams. The key idea is to instantiate a VICReg-style objective with temporally adjacent positives and non-differentiated running population statistics, yielding a per-neuron online loss with bounded state. The objective is a soft form of Slow Feature Analysis, and its gradient is a Hebbian update of the feedforward weights and an anti-Hebbian update of one lateral matrix per layer. The aim of the experiments is to show that the rule works in a small network, not to compete with backpropagation. On a class-chunked MNIST stream, a two-layer fully connected network trained with batch size one outperforms random features (96.48% versus 95.09% linear-probe accuracy) and classical SFA, and a variant that relaxes both locality constraints is comparable to supervised backpropagation. Because training and inference use the same computation, the network can keep learning from unlabeled data during inference without loss of accuracy.

2611.17007.abs: Large language model (LLM) agents use external skills to reuse task procedures and experience with tools. General-purpose skills describe shared execution procedures, while specific tool choices, operating practices, and output requirements vary across users. In long-horizon tasks, subgoals, available inputs, and environmental states change as execution progresses. Agents must select currently applicable skills from an expanding skill pool and prepare candidates for subsequent steps. We propose Skill Adapter, which enables personalized modification and online routing of general-purpose skills. The system distills local adjustments from user requirements and execution feedback and stores them as Adapters linked to general-purpose skills. The routing agent selects general-purpose skills and applicable Adapters based on the current subtask, execution progress, and environmental feedback, incrementally maintaining a task-level online skill library that the main LLM reads on demand. The system preloads candidates for subsequent nodes and rechecks their applicability once actual inputs are determined. Reinforcement learning optimizes the two types of decisions using modification gains and routing outcomes, respectively. We evaluate Skill Adapter on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SkillsBench. Compared with SkillRL, it improves task success rates by an average of 11.43 percentage points and reduces mean execution time on all three benchmarks. Skill Adapter retains its performance advantage when the skill pool grows to 1,000 skills.

2611.16981.abs: Weight-space programming (WSP) uses language models to construct neural network weights without training. We test whether known game mechanics can be compiled into compact agents that generalise to held-out levels, renderings and start states within a game family. Writers receive simulator source with held-out level data removed for 20 privately authored, unpublished ARC-AGI-3-style game families. With a fixed 57k-parameter recurrent architecture, the strongest writer reaches 56% held-out-level success with feedback, while the four main writers' Python players reach 97-100%. An exploratory free-architecture condition reaches 68-90%. Learning from support-level examples transfers much less well, but these learners lack the source information given to writers. Written networks have a program-like structure: 93% of parameters are zero, and 90% of the rest are small integers or powers of two. NumPy players under comparable computation caps reach 91%, versus the networks' 79%. Training the strongest writer's architectures from scratch yields about 1% success within our budget. Written fixed-network weights are fragile, and standard PPO removes most of their success. Prompts for noise robustness increase tolerance by about four orders of magnitude for two of three writers, but PPO makes larger updates and still removes most success. These results demonstrate rule-to-network compilation in this setting, while showing limited benefits over Python programs and no successful combination with the tested PPO fine-tuning.

ov.problema: La programmazione nello spazio dei pesi (WSP) usa modelli linguistici per costruire pesi di reti neurali senza addestramento. Si vuole testare se meccaniche di gioco note possano essere compilate in agenti compatti che generalizzano a livelli, rendering e stati iniziali non visti all'interno di una famiglia di giochi.
ov.idea: Gli autori forniscono a scrittori (modelli linguistici) il codice sorgente del simulatore con i dati dei livelli tenuti nascosti per 20 famiglie di giochi in stile ARC-AGI-3, private e non pubblicate. Usano un'architettura ricorrente fissa da 57k parametri. Gli scrittori generano i pesi della rete neurale che funge da agente. Confrontano con giocatori Python scritti dagli stessi modelli.
ov.risultati: Il miglior scrittore raggiunge il 56% di successo su livelli tenuti nascosti con feedback, mentre i giocatori Python dei quattro principali scrittori raggiungono il 97-100%. Una condizione esplorativa con architettura libera raggiunge il 68-90%. Le reti scritte hanno una struttura simile a un programma: il 93% dei parametri è zero e il 90% del resto sono piccoli interi o potenze di due. I giocatori NumPy sotto limiti di calcolo comparabili raggiungono il 91%, contro il 79% delle reti. Addestrare da zero le architetture del miglior scrittore dà circa l'1% di successo nel budget. I pesi scritti…
ov.limiti: I pesi scritti sono fragili e il PPO rimuove gran parte del successo; inoltre, i giocatori Python superano le reti, e non c'è una combinazione di successo con altri metodi.

glossario.d: Tecnica che usa modelli linguistici per generare direttamente i pesi di una rete neurale senza addestramento.
Terza edizione di una serie di benchmark per l'intelligenza artificiale generale, con compiti di ragionamento astratto.
Proximal Policy Optimization: algoritmo di apprendimento per rinforzo che aggiorna la politica in modo controllato.

2611.16881.abs: Protein language models (pLMs) produce highly accurate contact maps from single-sequence inputs. People often take this accuracy as proof that these models implicitly learn invariant coevolutionary statistics, extracting the same signals as classical alignment-based methods like Potts. In this work, we introduce a diagnostic framework around a global bijective relabeling of the amino-acid alphabet. This transformation permutes residue letters while leaving all alignment-level information, column entropies, and pairwise edit distances unchanged. Pseudolikelihood Potts models and inverse-covariance estimators remain invariant under this transformation, but pLMs fail the test. Across multiple architectures (ESM-2, MSA Transformer, AMPLIFY) and model scales (8M to 3B parameters), pLM contact maps collapse under arbitrary relabeling. Using Hamming distance controls and biochemical grouping interventions, we attempt to isolate what likely causes this degradation and find that these models rely on explicit, canonical residue identities (``alphabet anchoring'') rather than pure coevolutionary statistics. Increasing scale makes models more responsive to biochemical classes, but their performance still degrades under relabeling. Our findings show a gap between how pLMs and classical coevolutionary models compute contacts. More broadly, our work shows how diagnostic perturbations that leave classical models provably unchanged can expose hidden representation biases and prevent over-reliance on neural black boxes in biological modeling.

2611.16677.abs: Generating scientific data under previously unseen equality constraints requires satisfying the prescribed constraints without destroying the physical structure learned from data. Existing inference-time approaches often enforce physical constraints by repeatedly correcting predicted endpoints, but such discrete corrections can distort learned generative structure and introduce unstable feedback. In this work, we propose Manifold Attracting Flow Matching (MAFM), which continuously evolves a persistent anchor through an ODE whose dynamics drive it analytically toward the constraint manifold. Specifically, its geometric correction preserves model-guided tangent motion while prescribing the normal motion to contract constraint violations toward the manifold. This construction separates model tracking from constraint attraction and provides theoretical guarantees for residual contraction and local feedback stabilization. Experiments across geometric and partial differential equation benchmarks demonstrate improved generation quality over variant constraint-guided baselines while maintaining low constraint residuals. MAFM provides a flexible framework for coordinating learned physical structure and explicit constraints through controllable sampling dynamics, without retraining the underlying generative model.

2611.16991.abs: Coding agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in software development, yet their ability to tackle long-horizon engineering tasks governed by physical constraints remains less understood. We study this question through analog circuit layout, which demands domain knowledge, geometric reasoning, and iterative interaction with design and verification tools. We introduce \textbf{AnalogLayoutWorld}, an open-source agent benchmark with 40 expert-reviewed tasks for end-to-end layout generation from fixed transistor-level netlists. It combines an integrated design environment with independent physical and post-layout electrical verification, as well as objective layout quality metrics co-designed with analog layout experts. Across 13 model--harness configurations, 91.1\% of attempts produce GDS layouts, but only 23.0\% satisfy the benchmark's acceptance criteria. We also evaluate Novara, an internally developed agent system, which achieves the highest reported aggregate score. Our analysis links performance differences to test-time scaling under fixed budgets, suggesting that reasoning efficiency and effective use of verification feedback help sustain design quality as task complexity grows.

ov.problema: Gli agenti di coding hanno forti capacità nello sviluppo software, ma la loro abilità in compiti ingegneristici a lungo termine governati da vincoli fisici è meno compresa. Lo studio affronta il layout di circuiti analogici, che richiede conoscenza di dominio, ragionamento geometrico e interazione iterativa con strumenti di progettazione e verifica.
ov.idea: Gli autori introducono AnalogLayoutWorld, un benchmark open-source per agenti con 40 compiti revisionati da esperti per la generazione end-to-end di layout da netlist a livello di transistor fissati. Combina un ambiente di progettazione integrato con verifica fisica ed elettrica post-layout indipendente, più metriche oggettive di qualità del layout co-progettate con esperti di layout analogico. Valutano anche Novara, un sistema agente sviluppato internamente.
ov.risultati: Su 13 configurazioni modello-harness, il 91.1% dei tentativi produce layout GDS, ma solo il 23.0% soddisfa i criteri di accettazione del benchmark. Novara raggiunge il punteggio aggregato più alto riportato. L'analisi collega le differenze di prestazioni al test-time scaling sotto budget fissi, suggerendo che l'efficienza di ragionamento e l'uso efficace del feedback di verifica aiutano a mantenere la qualità al crescere della complessità.
ov.limiti: Il testo non elenca limiti espliciti, ma la bassa percentuale di accettazione (23.0%) indica che i compiti sono ancora molto difficili per gli agenti attuali.

glossario.d: Descrizione delle connessioni tra componenti elettronici in un circuito.
Formato di file standard per layout di circuiti integrati, usato nella produzione di chip.
Aumento della capacità di calcolo o del numero di tentativi durante l'esecuzione per migliorare le prestazioni.

2611.16986.abs: Educational simulations are a well-established pedagogical technique that gives learners opportunities to apply knowledge, respond to challenges, and reflect on their performance. High-quality simulations, however, are difficult to build, requiring instructor input, scenario design, character development, scaffolding, technical implementation, and repeated revision. This paper presents Primer, an open-source, LLM-agnostic AI-supported system that helps educators create adaptive educational simulations. Educators contribute their knowledge of the subject, lesson, and students, while generative AI produces responsive variations of practice for students. Primer uses a multi-agent system centered around executing educator's instructional intent through the entire learning experience. We hope that by releasing Primer as an open-source system, including its prompts and GitHub repository, we provide a foundation for development and research on educator-in-the-loop AI authoring, multi-agent educational workflows, and simulation-based pedagogy. Further, by allowing the use of various AI models, including local and open source models, we provide the opportunity for implementation under varied governance regimes. Primer points toward a model of educational AI in which instructors can create locally grounded practice opportunities based on their own materials, goals, examples, and knowledge of students.

2611.16984.abs: Vision transformers (ViTs) serve as the backbone for countless vision tasks, including dense prediction tasks, such as segmentation and depth estimation, even though the quadratic complexity of self-attention severely limits feature resolution and induces spatial artifacts. In this work, we introduce ElasticDino, a lightweight adapter which produces high-resolution feature maps, adhering to the fine details of the input image. As a key insight, we observe the consistency of artifacts across channels, and simultaneously resolve them to match the input image structure. Using a slim architecture based on spatial deformations, ElasticDino produces pixel-aligned, high-resolution feature maps efficiently. Leveraging deformations allows strictly preserving sharp semantics, and thereby avoiding the smoothness biases inherent to alternative approaches. Due to the absence of ground truth, we employ pixel-level semantic segmentation and depth estimation with linear heads to predict a set of downstream dense tasks, guiding the deformation process without leaking task-specific semantics into the model. We demonstrate superior accuracy over current methods on a range of popular dense task benchmarks, with better computational performance.

2611.16937.abs: Typed System-1 (S1) decision models are increasingly deployed in LLM agents for routing, moderation, and authorization to cut inference cost, yet untrusted context can still manipulate typed outputs and alter execution branches. Unlike autoregressive System-2 (S2) models, S1 interfaces score dynamic rules and options without token-by-token decoding, mismatching attacks targeting text continuation or explicit override commands. We propose S1-Evo, a self-evolving framework tailored to S1's contract-based option competition and margin feedback. S1-Evo perturbs untrusted fields via contract-aware evidence channels to induce \emph{evidence competition} with original task evidence while preserving fact invariance. Offline on seed tasks, it optimizes candidates via feedback search guided by directional margins and re-verification, distilling verified flips into experience cards. At test time, S1-Evo retrieves relevant cards to construct perturbations for unseen tasks. Across four benchmarks and three S1 models, S1-Evo reaches 71.99\% mean ASR and 57.47\% high-confidence ASR on \texttt{jev-1.14}, and causes up to 24.00\% E2E agent violations.

2611.16882.abs: How does data shape language model (LM) behavior throughout pretraining? We investigate this question through a case study on entity comparison, e.g., Between France and Brazil, which country is larger?, across nine comparison tasks spanning five entity types. We begin with controlled experiments in which we train small LMs (163M parameters) on mixtures of natural text from pretraining corpora and synthetic task data. Our analysis identifies three distinct phases of learning: (1) an early phase where the LM selects entities by frequency, (2) a middle phase where the LM selects entities by position in the prompt (first vs. last mentioned entity), and (3) a late phase where the LM selects the entity that is the correct answer. We show that the emergence of these three phases is causally determined by statistical properties of the training data. With small amounts of task-specific synthetic data, we observe only the first two phases and the model fails to learn the task; with large amounts, the model jumps directly from the frequency-based heuristic to solving the task correctly. Moreover, changing the entity frequency distribution from a naturally occurring Zipfian distribution (a small number of entities are very common and the vast majority are rare) to a uniform one weakens the frequency phase and speeds up learning of the task. Lastly, we show that the three phases of training dynamics from our controlled experiments appear in the open source model OLMo-2 32B. Together, our findings demonstrate that properties of pretraining data are causal drivers of heuristic learning…

ov.problema: Come i dati di pre-addestramento plasmano il comportamento dei modelli linguistici nel tempo? Lo studiano sul caso concreto del confronto tra entità (es. quale paese è più grande).
ov.idea: Addestrano piccoli LM (163M parametri) su miscele di testo naturale e dati sintetici specifici. Identificano tre fasi: selezione per frequenza, poi per posizione nel prompt, infine per risposta corretta. Le fasi dipendono causalmente dalle proprietà statistiche dei dati.
ov.risultati: Con pochi dati sintetici compaiono solo le prime due fasi e il modello fallisce; con molti dati salta direttamente dalla frequenza alla soluzione corretta. Cambiare la distribuzione di frequenza da Zipfiana a uniforme indebolisce la fase di frequenza e accelera l'apprendimento. Le tre fasi appaiono anche in OLMo-2 32B.

glossario.d: Pochissimi elementi molto frequenti e moltissimi rari, tipica del linguaggio naturale.
Periodo dell'addestramento in cui il modello usa una specifica euristica.

2611.16872.abs: Recent advances in frontier models have pushed the boundaries of agentic robot control, enabling agents to perform complex robotic tasks through reasoning and interaction. However, repeated calls to these models during execution can substantially increase task completion time. Code as Policies (CaP) offers a route for coding agents to acquire physical skills through experience and retain them in executable programs, allowing the reasoning invested in development to be reused across runs. Developing reliable code policies while limiting the cost of physical experimentation remains a central challenge. We investigate human guidance as a source of priors for feasible actions and simulation as an auxiliary environment for exploring and testing candidate policies. Our findings favor robot demonstrations available on request and simulation used selectively during real-world policy refinement. These findings inform ACE-CaP-0, an agentic recipe that couples policy revision with experience acquisition through Demonstrations on Request and Simulation on Demand. Across eight real-world manipulation tasks spanning alignment, multi-object handling, and bimanual coordination, the resulting frozen programs achieve 92.1\% success (221/240 trials). Mean execution times across tasks range from 0.97 to 2.27 minutes. The programs execute with runtime perception and control, without a human or coding agent in the loop. These results highlight CaP's potential to turn experience into reliable, reusable physical skills.

2611.17105.abs: Combining vision-language models (VLMs) with parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) offers a promising approach to few-shot whole-slide image (WSI) classification in computational pathology. This study evaluates this approach for predicting ethanol drinking status from nonhuman primate liver histology. Adapters are evaluated against non-PEFT configurations on a subset of the Monkey Alcohol Tissue Research Resource (MATRR). All evaluated PEFT configurations achieve higher mean balanced accuracy than the non-PEFT baselines. For example, in the four-shot setting, attention-based multiple instance learning (ABMIL) alone achieves 43.5% mean balanced accuracy, compared with 78.1% after adding an adapter. Qualitative attention analysis shows that textual pathway adaptations produce localized attention heatmaps, while visual pathway adaptations produce more diffuse ones. A pathologist's review identified similar histological features across adaptations.

2611.17103.abs: Merging independently fine-tuned checkpoints into a single multi-task model requires no data, no labels, and no gradient steps. In practice the task vectors of different tasks interfere, and the standard remedies--averaging, magnitude pruning, sign election--operate entry by entry, ignoring that each delta induces a low-dimensional update on the hidden features it acts upon. We recast merging as a subspace interference problem. For every two-dimensional weight tensor we take the top-r right-singular subspace of each task's delta--the input directions along which that task moves the representation most--and remove from each task vector the component lying in the union of the other tasks' subspaces. The resulting Joint Null-Space Projection (JNSP) is closed-form and order-independent, needs no forward pass, and is defined entirely by the checkpoint set. On eight CLIP image-classification tasks JNSP merges ViT-B/16 experts to 89.45% average accuracy without using a single image, 11.88 points above the strongest parameter-wise training-free baseline (TIES-Merging, 77.57%), 14.22 above Task Arithmetic, and 0.98 above WUDI's data-free consensus merge (88.47%). The gain holds across three backbones on the independently trained TALL release (+10.8, +12.6, +9.1 over TIES for ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14) and replicates there at 89.20%; controls confirm the source--a single shared subspace instead of per-task ones loses 2.9 points, and a sequential variant collapses to 69.6%. On RoBERTa-large the same projection underperforms plain task arithmetic, which we report rather than hide.…

ov.problema: Unire più modelli fine-tuned (adattati a compiti diversi) in un unico modello multi-compito senza usare dati, etichette o gradienti è difficile perché i vettori dei compiti interferiscono tra loro. I metodi standard operano elemento per elemento, ignorando che ogni modifica induce un aggiornamento a bassa dimensionalità sulle feature nascoste.
ov.idea: Gli autori riformulano il merging come un problema di interferenza tra sottospazi. Per ogni tensore di peso bidimensionale, prendono il sottospazio delle direzioni di input lungo cui ogni compito muove maggiormente la rappresentazione (tramite decomposizione ai valori singolari) e rimuovono da ciascun vettore di compito la componente che giace nell'unione dei sottospazi degli altri compiti. Il metodo risultante, Joint Null-Space Projection (JNSP), è in forma chiusa, indipendente dall'ordine e non richiede forward pass.
ov.risultati: Su otto compiti di classificazione di immagini CLIP, JNSP unisce esperti ViT-B/16 raggiungendo l'89.45% di accuratezza media senza usare immagini, 11.88 punti sopra il miglior baseline training-free (TIES-Merging, 77.57%), 14.22 sopra Task Arithmetic e 0.98 sopra WUDI (88.47%). Il guadagno si mantiene su tre backbone nella release TALL (+10.8, +12.6, +9.1 su TIES per ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14) e replica a 89.20%. Controlli mostrano che un singolo sottospazio condiviso perde 2.9 punti e una variante sequenziale crolla a 69.6%.
ov.limiti: Il testo menziona che i risultati su RoBERTa sono troncati, quindi non è possibile valutare appieno le prestazioni su altri domini.

glossario.d: Differenza tra i pesi di un modello fine-tuned e quelli del modello pre-addestrato, che rappresenta l'adattamento al compito.
Insieme di direzioni in uno spazio vettoriale che può essere descritto da una combinazione lineare di pochi vettori base.
Tecnica che scompone una matrice in componenti ordinate per importanza, usata per ridurre dimensionalità.

2611.17091.abs: Provably secure linguistic steganography assumes that the receiver recovers the sender's tokens, but a text channel delivers only text, and ambiguous tokenizations break extraction. Existing fixes change the distribution, synchronize whole pools of tokens at a capacity that collapses with large vocabularies, or track several token histories. We prove that if extraction is exact and error-free across full-support language models, a single-history receiver is confined to a prefix-free candidate set at every step -- even if it reads the entire future text and the sender constrains later steps -- and must therefore give up the stop entropy, the entropy of deciding whether each prefix token ends there. Fixing these stop decisions on the prefix forest with shared randomness yields coin projection: a closed-form scheme that attains the bound, works with any distribution coder in one model call per token, preserves ordinary sampling, and refines SyncPool for every key. Across English, Chinese and Japanese, ambiguous text is rare (at most 11 in 1,000 tokens), yet the stop entropy at word and morpheme prefixes takes 7.2-9.0% of the entropy at every step; SyncPool's further loss comes from space and single-byte UTF-8 hubs that merge subtrees while carrying almost no stop uncertainty. Coin projection keeps 91-93% of the string entropy for the coder at every vocabulary size; with the full vocabulary, it turns 2.16-6.85 times as much entropy into message bits as SyncPool and recovers every completed message.

2611.16803.abs: Many failures of language models begin at a specific token, the onset. A monitor that reads the model during generation can classify the finished response, detect the failure once it is under way, or warn before it begins, and only a warning leaves time to stop or steer the generation. Monitors are usually evaluated with response-level metrics such as AUROC, which ignore when the monitor fires. We introduce PREWARN, an evaluation protocol for any failure with an annotated onset. It calibrates each monitor's threshold on validation data to an error rate chosen for the application, runs the monitor, and scores its alarms relative to the onset on all three tasks. As a case study we apply it to repetitive degeneration in three open language models, with early warning as the main task, using linear probes on activations and six untrained baselines. Response-level metrics saturate on this failure, and a rule that reads only the response length scores almost perfectly, while probes that AUROC ranks as equal warn very differently under PREWARN. Probes warn before the onset on most degenerate responses of two of the three models, low-rank adapters below the probe more than double the share of tokens just before the onset that it flags, largely by flagging degenerate responses long before the onset, and no untrained baseline warns much more often than random alarms. We release the probes with calibrated thresholds at https://huggingface.co/collections/marcodene/prewarn-degeneration-probes

ov.problema: Molti fallimenti dei modelli linguistici iniziano a un token specifico, l'onset. Un monitor che legge il modello durante la generazione può classificare la risposta finita, rilevare il fallimento una volta in corso, o avvisare prima che inizi; solo un avviso lascia tempo per fermare o guidare la generazione. I monitor sono di solito valutati con metriche a livello di risposta come AUROC, che ignorano quando il monitor scatta.
ov.idea: PREWARN è un protocollo di valutazione per qualsiasi fallimento con un onset annotato. Calibra la soglia di ogni monitor su dati di validazione a un tasso di errore scelto per l'applicazione, esegue il monitor e valuta i suoi allarmi rispetto all'onset su tutti e tre i task (classificazione, rilevamento, preavviso). Come caso di studio, lo applica alla degenerazione ripetitiva in tre modelli linguistici aperti, con preavviso come task principale, usando sonde lineari su attivazioni e sei baseline non addestrate.
ov.risultati: Le metriche a livello di risposta saturano su questo fallimento e una regola che legge solo la lunghezza della risposta ottiene quasi il punteggio perfetto, mentre sonde che AUROC classifica come uguali avvisano molto diversamente sotto PREWARN. Le sonde avvisano prima dell'onset sulla maggior parte delle risposte degeneri di due dei tre modelli; adattatori a basso rango sotto la sonda più che raddoppiano la quota di token appena prima dell'onset che essa segnala, in gran parte segnalando risposte degeneri molto prima dell'onset; nessuna baseline non addestrata avvisa molto più spesso di…
ov.limiti: Lo studio è limitato alla degenerazione ripetitiva e a tre modelli aperti; i risultati potrebbero non generalizzare ad altri fallimenti.

glossario.d: Token specifico in cui inizia un fallimento.
Area sotto la curva ROC: metrica di classificazione binaria.
Classificatore lineare addestrato su attivazioni interne del modello.

2611.17053.abs: Structured Electronic Health Records (EHR) models typically treat each clinical concept as a dataset-specific token, discarding the natural-language semantics associated with the event. As a result, relationships between concepts must largely be learned from EHR co-occurrence, without directly exploiting any prior semantic knowledge. We investigate how pretrained causal language models can be adapted for longitudinal EHR prediction by developing tEHR. Here, we represent events with their natural language description and use this text stream to apply EHR-adaptive continued pretraining, followed by task-specific discriminative fine-tuning using LoRA, utilising the LLM as a longitudinal patient-encoder. We evaluate this approach across four prediction tasks on the MIMIC-IV dataset and pancreatic cancer prediction on the CPRD dataset at 1 to 12 month horizons, with tEHR using the Mistral-7B-v0.3 backbone achieving the strongest overall performance. Ablations show that performance declines when clinical descriptions are removed or misaligned, when numerical values are omitted, and when either stage of adaptation is removed, while explicit elapsed-time descriptions provide little additional benefit. Analysis of the learned patient representations further reveals clinically coherent structure associated with distinct patterns of disease risk and clinical history.

2611.17042.abs: Users of artificial intelligence services, including those powered by large language models and other transformer-based models, need assurance that inference and training follow the declared computation without exposing private models or data. Zero-knowledge proofs can provide this assurance, but proof generation remains expensive. Hardware acceleration research often reports gains for individual cryptographic operations, leaving their effect on the full cost of proving neural-network workloads, particularly large transformer models, unclear. We introduce a four-layer framework linking verifiable AI workloads, proof systems, cryptographic kernels and hardware platforms, use it to review the literature, and add original measurements of six provers and seven kernels to identify which costs matter in practice. Our measurements show that the dominant cost changes with the proof system and input length. In low-rank fine-tuning, the cost of opening commitments to fixed model weights remains nearly constant across input lengths from 64 to 2048, while the work associated with intermediate values grows. A 13-billion-parameter fine-tuning configuration exceeds the capacity of a 40-gigabyte graphics processor but completes on an 80-gigabyte device, showing why capacity must be assessed alongside execution time. Our kernel profiling further identifies instruction issue and synchronization limits that a bandwidth-only model misses. We use these findings to assess graphics processors, reconfigurable logic, custom chips and existing artificial intelligence accelerators. The resulting…

2611.16934.abs: Time series foundation models have demonstrated strong zero-shot forecasting performance, but computational efficiency remains a central architectural challenge. Temporal self-attention incurs quadratic cost in the number of temporal tokens, while nonlinear recurrent state transitions restrict parallel computation along the temporal dimension. We introduce ci-proto, a family of time series foundation models based on Mamba-3, whose linear state recurrences support chunk-wise parallel-in-time computation during training, and inference costs that scale linearly with sequence length. The architecture alternates recurrent temporal processing with cross-variate attention, supporting multivariate probabilistic forecasting with past-only and future-known covariates. Across fev-bench's 100 forecasting tasks, ci-proto XL sets a new state of the art among time series foundation models. The five ci-proto variants also make up the entire Pareto frontier for mean scaled quantile loss and mean absolute scaled error against both parameter count and median runtime.

ov.problema: I modelli fondazionali per serie temporali (modelli pre-addestrati su grandi quantità di dati per fare previsioni) sono potenti ma costosi: l'attenzione temporale cresce col quadrato della lunghezza, e le ricorrenze non lineari impediscono il calcolo parallelo lungo il tempo.
ov.idea: Introducono ci-proto, basato su Mamba-3: ricorrenze di stato lineari che permettono calcolo parallelo a blocchi durante l'addestramento e costo di inferenza lineare nella lunghezza. L'architettura alterna elaborazione temporale ricorrente e attenzione tra variabili, supportando previsioni multivariate probabilistiche con covariate passate e future note.
ov.risultati: Su 100 task di fev-bench, ci-proto XL raggiunge il nuovo stato dell'arte tra i modelli fondazionali per serie temporali. Le cinque varianti ci-proto occupano l'intera frontiera di Pareto per mean scaled quantile loss e mean absolute scaled error rispetto a parametri e runtime mediano.

glossario.d: Architettura a spazio di stato con ricorrenze lineari, alternativa efficiente all'attenzione.
